sections.hypothesis: btc-regime-trend, unchanged from its confirmation run (BTC above its 50-day average and the coin up over 30 days, sized to 50% volatility), beats holding ETH and SOL at the same exposure on Sharpe after costs, daily bars.
sections.rationale: The rule passed the exploration experiment's confirmation on 180 unsearched altcoins (findings item 13). ETH and SOL were left out of that split because they are Kestrel's most-searched coins, so this is not a confirmation: it is Luke's question whether the altcoin rule also works on the two large coins Kestrel already paper-trades with trend-vol-target. It leans on BTC's trend, as trend-vol-target does, so the useful comparison is with trend-vol-target on the same coins (Sharpe 1.24 on ETH 2020-25 and 1.52 on SOL 2020-08 to 2025-10, from their scorecard note). Nothing is tuned.
sections.rules: btc-regime-trend with its defaults (btc_days 50, coin_days 30, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50), daily bars, spot, long only, 330 USDT, costs from kestrel.toml. ETHUSDT 2020-01 to 2025-10; SOLUSDT 2020-08 to 2025-10. v1's two backtests stand (not rerun). v2 adds, for each coin: kestrel walk-forward (grid btc_days 30,50,100 x coin_days 10,30,60; 24-month train, 6-month test, as for BTC's trend standard) and kestrel robustness around the defaults. All before the holdout.
sections.falsification: The full scorecard on each coin with v1's runs: test 3 needs most walk-forward test windows to beat holding; test 8 needs at least 80% of neighbouring settings to beat holding's Sharpe (the plateau rule). Luck stays graded against the main bar. Claude decides watch or pursue from the result (Luke, 2026-11-16): pursue would mean forward paper trading on the testnet beside trend-vol-target, since both coins' holdout years are spent.
sections.parameters: The defaults, fixed for the backtests. The walk-forward grid above (9 points a coin) and the robustness neighbours are the only other settings run.
sections.costs: As v1. Trials: about 9 grid points and about 15 neighbours a coin, about 50 in all, in the main pool.

change_reason: v1 ran test 1 only (2026-11-16): it passed on both coins. Luke asked to finish the scorecard: walk-forward and robustness on the same coins, periods and rule, nothing tuned.
